title: Survey on Evaluation of LLM-based Agents
abstract: This survey provides a comprehensive overview of evaluation methodologies for LLM-based agents, focusing on four foundational capabilities: planning, function calling, self-reflection, and memory. We analyze benchmarks and frameworks across critical dimensions and identify emerging trends and gaps for future research.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're building a robot that can plan and adapt to new situations. LLM-based agents are like these robots, but for language tasks. They can plan, use tools, and even reflect on their own performance. But how do we evaluate their abilities?

We need to assess their fundamental capabilities to understand their potential and limitations.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
LLM-based agents use multi-step reasoning to tackle complex tasks. They can decompose problems into smaller sub-tasks and create strategic execution paths. But how do we evaluate this process?

We use benchmarks like PlanBench and AutoPlanBench to assess their planning capabilities.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
We've seen significant progress in benchmark results for LLM-based agents. For example, ToolBench has achieved a pass rate of 85% on tool-use tasks. But there's still room for improvement.

We need to develop more challenging benchmarks to push the limits of LLM-based agents.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
Evaluating LLM-based agents is crucial for real-world applications. We need to ensure that these agents can plan, use tools, and reflect effectively in dynamic environments.

This has significant implications for fields like software engineering and scientific research.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
Recent innovations in LLM-based agents include self-reflection and memory mechanisms. These advancements enable agents to learn from feedback and retain context over extended interactions.

We've seen significant progress in benchmark development, with new benchmarks like LLF-Bench and ReadAgent.

sections.title: What Came Next
sections.content:
The future of LLM-based agents holds much promise. We can expect to see more advanced benchmarks and innovative applications in fields like conversational AI and scientific research.

As researchers and practitioners, we must continue to push the boundaries of what is possible with LLM-based agents.
